messages.subject: Specifying t-distributions on measurement part of SEM
messages.subject_clean: Specifying t-distributions on measurement part of SEM
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am new to blavaan and to bayesian SEM. I am trying to specify t-distributions on the below "measurement part" of my SEM:

> semmodel <- '
>
> # Measurement Part
> workshop =~ zeroneg+dialogqual+checkin+pgrpnumber
>
> # Regressions
> DAS_gain ~ A*workshop + B*FAD_gain + C*PSS_gain + CC*Trait_gain
> workshop ~ D*white + E*gender + G*jobstress + H*tools
> FAD_gain ~ I*gender + J*white + K*jobstress + L*PSS_gain + M*Trait_gain
> PSS_gain ~ N*white + O*gender + P*jobstress + Q*Trait_gain
> tools ~ R*white + S*gender + T*jobstress
> Trait_gain ~ U*white + V*gender + W*jobstress + X*tools + Y*workshop
>
> '
>
> # Unique priors for mv intercepts; parallel chains
> fit <- bsem(semmodel, data=dat2,
>             dp=dpriors(nu="dnorm(5,1e-2)"),
>             bcontrol=list(method="rjparallel"))
> summary(fit)

I have read the blavaan article on exporting into jags, but have not been successful at running both the measurement and regression syntax.

Is there a way to specify t-distributions all in rjags without using blavaan? I'm also curious why using the "=~" measurement syntax doesn't work in the below.

Here is what I currently have (curtailed in some redundant places to save space):

> modelstring = "
>
> model {
> for (i in 1:nData)
> {
>
> ##Distribution for the outcome (DAS_gain; changes in relationship satisfaction)
> DAS_gain[i]~dnorm(mu1[i],tau1)
>
> ##Model for DAS_gain
> mu1[i]<-a0 + a1*workshop[i] + a2*FAD_gain[i]+ a3*PSS_gain[i] + a4*Trait_gain
>
> ##Distrubution and model for Workshop
> workshop[i]~dnorm(mu2[i], tau2)
> mu2[i]<-b0 + b1*white[i] + b2*gender[i] + b3*jobstress[i] + b4*tools[i]

> ##Distribution and model for FAD_gain
> FAD_gain[i]~dnorm(mu3[i], tau3)
> mu3[i]<-c0 + c1*gender[i] + c2*white[i] + c3*jobstress[i] + c4*PSS_gain[i] + c5*Trait_gain[i]
>
> ##Distribution and model for PSS_gain
> PSS_gain[i]~dnorm(mu4[i], tau4)
> mu4[i]<-d0 + d1*white[i] + d2*gender[i] + d3*jobstress[i] + d4*Trait_gain[i]

           ...and so on

> }
>
> #--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
> # Priors on regression coefficients - normal weakly informative
> a0 ~ dnorm(200,.01)
> a1 ~ dnorm(5,.01)
> a2 ~ dnorm(5,.01)
> a3 ~ dnorm(5,.01)
> a4 ~ dnorm(5,.01)
> b0 ~ dnorm(5,.01)
> b1 ~ dnorm(1,.01)
> b2 ~ dnorm(1,.01)
> b3 ~ dnorm(1,.01)
> b4 ~ dnorm(1,.01)
> c0 ~ dnorm(5,.01)
> c1 ~ dnorm(1,.01)
> c2 ~ dnorm(1,.01)
> c3 ~ dnorm(1,.01)
           ...and so on
>
> # Priors on Precisions - gamma non-informative
> tau1 ~ dgamma(0.01,0.01)
> tau2 ~ dgamma(0.01,0.01)
> tau3 ~ dgamma(0.01,0.01)
> tau4 ~ dgamma(0.01,0.01)
> tau5 ~ dgamma(0.01,0.01)
> tau6 ~ dgamma(0.01,0.01)
> tau7 ~ dgamma(0.01,0.01)
           ...and so on
>
> }
> "
> ```

Any advice is appreciated! Thank you.
Bayesian Structural Equation Models - arXiv <https://arxiv.org/pdf/1511.05604>

messages.body_plain:
Travis,

I assume that you saw around Fig 4 of the blavaan paper, which shows
how to insert t distributions in the jags code? If not, that section
hopefully provides some help.

I don't immediately see problems with the code that you posted, but it
is also hard to say without a full example. I would first try running
your desired model (except without t distributions) using the bsem
command, to make sure that works. Then export the jags syntax from
that working model, then edit in the t distributions.

Would also be good to make sure you have the latest blavaan version on
CRAN (0.3-3), which contains some bug fixes.

Best,
Ed

messages.subject: Setting uniform prior on specific error covariance
messages.subject_clean: Setting uniform prior on specific error covariance
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ed,

Consider the model below:

model <- '
    x ~ lzx*z
    y ~ lxy*x
    w ~ lzw*z

    x ~~ cxz*z
    y ~~ cyz*z
    w ~~ cwz*z
    y ~~ cwy*w'

Is there an easy way I can put a uniform prior, say [-.2, .2] on the error covariance cwz?

Relatedly, does the package provide a function for plowing prior vs posterior distribution of a parameter?

Thanks.

Best, Carlos

messages.subject: Re: Setting uniform prior on specific error covariance
messages.subject_clean: Setting uniform prior on specific error covariance
messages.body_plain:
Carlos,

Regarding the prior on the covariance: blavaan breaks up the
covariance into something like

sd_1 * sd_2 * corr_12

and then you put a prior on these three terms (the two
variances/standard deviations/precisions, along with the correlation).
So it is easy to put a prior on the correlation, but not the
covariance. But there is a trick here: the correlation is between -1
and 1, but there are few distributions with support on (-1,1). So you
have to use a distribution with support between 0 and 1 (typically
beta distribution), which is then automatically translated to a
distribution with support on (-1,1).

But this is a little funny for a uniform prior. In that case, you have
to figure out that uniform(.4,.6) on (0,1) becomes uniform(-.2,.2) on
(-1,1). So the syntax would look like

w ~~ cwz*z + prior("dunif(.4,.6)")*z

And then you might still have trouble with initial values, because any
(random) starting value outside of (-.2,.2) might crash the model. In
this case, maybe try the option inits="simple". But I would recommend
instead using a beta prior where most of the density lies between .4
and .6 under (0,1) support.

Re plotting: there is currently no automatic way to plot prior vs
posterior. I notice the bayesplot package makes some of the plotting
stuff easier but have not explored it much yet.

Ed

messages.subject: Error in plot function
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I have a simple Markov model defined as:

library(tidyverse)
library(blavaan)

lg <- read.csv("PrmLg17_18.csv", header = TRUE, row.names = 1)

mm <- '
Week4 ~ Week1
Week8 ~ Week4
Week11 ~ Week8
Week15 ~ Week11
Week22 ~ Week15
Week26 ~ Week22
Week29 ~ Week26
Week33 ~ Week29
Week37 ~ Week33
Week38 ~ Week37'

a <- bsem(mm, data = lg, n.chains = 4, bcontrol = list(cores = parallel::detectCores()))

plot(a, pars= 1:4, plot.type="autocorr") #Autocorrelation plots

plot(a, pars= 1:4, plot.type="ecdf") #ECDF plots

plot(a, pars= 1:4, plot.type="density") #Density plots

#PS: I am using stan, and anytime I try to run these plot functions, I get an error, usually
> plot(a, pars= 1:4, plot.type="autocorr") #Autocorrelation plots
Error in .local(x, ...) : Plotting function not found.

The plot function only seem to work for:
plot(a, pars= 1:4, plot.type="trace") #Traceplots

I'll be glad if you can help

Thanks,
John

messages.subject: Re: Error in plot function
messages.body_plain:
John,

The plot.type options differ between jags and stan, because the
blavaan plot command is just a wrapper around the runjags and rstan
plot commands. For stan, the plot.type can be any word after the "_"
in this list of options:

http://mc-stan.org/rstan/reference/plotting-functions.html

e.g., "plot", "trace", "hist", etc

Ed

messages.subject: Re: Setting uniform prior on specific error covariance
messages.subject_clean: Setting uniform prior on specific error covariance
messages.body_plain:
Thanks, Ed!

On Sunday, November 25, 2018 at 8:16:16 PM UTC-8, Ed Merkle wrote:
> Carlos,
>
> Regarding the prior on the covariance: blavaan breaks up the
> covariance into something like
>
> sd_1 * sd_2 * corr_12
>
> and then you put a prior on these three terms (the two
> variances/standard deviations/precisions, along with the correlation).
> So it is easy to put a prior on the correlation, but not the
> covariance. But there is a trick here: the correlation is between -1
> and 1, but there are few distributions with support on (-1,1). So you
> have to use a distribution with support between 0 and 1 (typically
> beta distribution), which is then automatically translated to a
> distribution with support on (-1,1).
>
> But this is a little funny for a uniform prior. In that case, you have
> to figure out that uniform(.4,.6) on (0,1) becomes uniform(-.2,.2) on
> (-1,1). So the syntax would look like
>
> w ~~ cwz*z + prior("dunif(.4,.6)")*z
>
> And then you might still have trouble with initial values, because any
> (random) starting value outside of (-.2,.2) might crash the model. In
> this case, maybe try the option inits="simple". But I would recommend
> instead using a beta prior where most of the density lies between .4
> and .6 under (0,1) support.
>
> Re plotting: there is currently no automatic way to plot prior vs
> posterior. I notice the bayesplot package makes some of the plotting
> stuff easier but have not explored it much yet.
>
> Ed
>
>
>
> On 11/25/18, Carlos Cinelli <carlosl...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > *plotting prior vs posterior distribution of a parameter?
> >
> > On Sunday, November 25, 2018 at 1:59:25 PM UTC-8, Carlos Cinelli wrote:

> >>     y ~ lxy*x
> >>     w ~ lzw*z
> >>
> >>     x ~~ cxz*z
> >>     y ~~ cyz*z
> >>     w ~~ cwz*z
> >>     y ~~ cwy*w'
> >>
> >>
> >> Is there an easy way I can put a uniform prior, say [-.2, .2] on the error
> >>
> >> covariance cwz?
> >>
> >> Relatedly, does the package provide a function for plowing prior vs

messages.subject: Standardised Priors
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am running a bsem model and using priors from a very similar study.

 I was wondering when I specify specific prior for a path, should I be specifying the beta from the original study or the unstandardized coefficient. And by extension, should the precision be based on the variance of the unstandardized or standardized coefficient?

If it is treating the prior as the unstandardized coefficient, is there a way to make blavaan use the standardized distribution as the beta?

Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: Standardised Priors
messages.body_plain:
Daniel,

blavaan models are estimated using "unstandardized" parameters, so
priors are always for unstandardized parameters. If you have an
informative prior for a standardized coefficient, maybe you could see
whether it is possible to translate this prior to an unstandardized
coefficient, based on what you know about the variance parameters in
the model. But there is not an automatic way to do this.

Ed

messages.subject: Re: Default priors and intercepts
messages.body_plain:
John,

This is a bit of a bug in the package: the parameters are being
treated as latent variable variances instead of observed variable
variances. (This is related to the way that the model is estimated,
where some observed variables are "upgraded" to latent variable
status.)

I will try to fix this soon. In the meantime, you can change those
priors in two ways. Either use "ipsi" instead of "itheta" in the
dpriors() command, or use the prior() modifier in the model syntax.

Regarding fixing the intercepts to 0, I think you need to use the
blavaan() command instead of bsem() to use int.ov.free. At least, the
behavior of blavaan seems to match the behavior of the lavaan sem()
command there.

Ed
